{{Infobox Election | election_name = United States House of Representatives election in North Dakota, At-large district, 2018 | country = North Dakota | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives election in North Dakota, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives election in North Dakota, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | election_date = November 6, 2018 | image1 = [[File:3x4.svg|x150px]] | nominee1 = [[Kelly Armstrong (politician)|Kelly Armstrong]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = [[File:Mac Schneider (cropped).jpg|x150px]] | nominee2 = [[Mac Schneider]] | party2 = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | image3 = | nominee3 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = Representative | before_election = [[Kevin Cramer]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{ElectionsND}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives election in North Dakota''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] for [[North Dakota's at-large congressional district]]. The election will coincide with the [[United States Senate election in North Dakota, 2018|U.S. Senate election]], as well as [[North Dakota elections, 2018|other statewide, legislative, and local elections]]. Though incumbent Republican U.S. Representative [[Kevin Cramer]] announced on January 11, 2018 he will run for re-election to a fourth term, he later indicated an intention to run for the Senate instead.{{cite news|url=http://www.politico.com/story/2016/11/2018-house-republicans-democratic-senators-showdown-231570|title=2018 showdown looms: House Republicans vs. Democratic senators|work=[[Politico]]|last1=Schor|first1=Elana|last2=Everett|first2=Burgess|date=November 18, 2016|accessdate=November 18, 2016}}{{cite news|last=Robillard|first=Kevin|title=Cramer won't run for Senate in North Dakota|date=January 11, 2018|newspaper=[[Politico]]|accessdate=January 11, 2018|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2018/01/11/kevin-cramer-no-senate-in-north-dakota-336495}}{{cite news|last1=Golshan|first1=Tara|title=A vulnerable North Dakota Democratic senator just attracted a serious GOP challenger|url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2018/2/15/17017438/cramer-heitkamp-north-dakota-senate|accessdate=February 15, 2018|work=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]|publisher=[[Vox Media]]|date=February 15, 2018}} On February 16, 2018, Cramer announced his Senate campaign. ==Republican primary== State Senator [[Tom Campbell (North Dakota politician)|Tom Campbell]] has stated he intends to run for the U.S. Senate if Cramer runs for re-election and to run for the U.S. House if Cramer does not run for re-election.{{cite news|url=http://www.grandforksherald.com/news/4164959-grafton-senator-eyes-congressional-run|title=Grafton senator eyes congressional run|work=[[Grand Forks Herald]]|last=Hageman|first=John|date=November 22, 2016|accessdate=November 23, 2016}} Campbell declared for the seat following Cramer's run for [[United States Senate election in North Dakota, 2018|Senate]]. However, on April 11, Campbell dropped out of the race to endorse Armstrong.https://www.rollcall.com/news/politics/tom-campbell-drops-north-dakota-house-race ===Candidates=== ====Nominated==== * [[Kelly M. Although general election ballot access is actually controlled by a Primary Election to be held June 12, both other candidates decided to withdraw from the race, rather than challenge Schneider in the primary.{{cite web|url=https://www.inforum.com/news/government-and-politics/4420062-hanson-endorses-fellow-nd-democrat-schneider-us-house-race|title=Hanson endorses fellow ND Democrat Mac Schneider in US House Race|work=[[Inforum]]|last=Hageman|first=John|date=March 20, 2018|accessdate=March 20, 2018}} ===Candidates=== ====Endorsed==== * [[Mac Schneider]], former Minority Leader of the [[North Dakota Senate]]{{cite web|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/4413515-mac-schneider-launches-us-house-bid-grand-forks|title=Mac Schneider launches U.S. House bid in Grand Forks|work=[[Grand Forks Herald]]|last=Easter|first=Sam|date=March 6, 2018|accessdate=March 6, 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/4419246-democrats-endorse-schneider-us-house-race|title=Democrats endorse Schneider for US House Race|work=[[Grand Forks Herald]]|last=Hageman|first=John|date=March 17, 2018|accessdate=March 17, 2018}} ====Withdrawn==== * [[Ben W. Hanson|Ben Hanson]], former State Representative{{cite web|url=http://kfgo.com/news/articles/2017/aug/16/ben-hanson-former-legislator-from-west-fargo-announces-bid-for-congress/|title=Ben Hanson, former legislator from West Fargo announces bid for congress|work=[[KFGO]]|last=Haney|first=Don|date=August 16, 2017|accessdate=August 16, 2017}} * [[John Grabinger]], State Senator{{cite web|url=https://www.jamestownsun.com/news/government-and-politics/4409182-grabinger-running-us-house|title=Grabinger running for U.S. House|work=[[The Jamestown Sun]]|last=Norman|first=Keith|date=February 26, 2018|accessdate=February 26, 2018}} ===Results=== [[File:2018 ND-AL Democratic primary.svg|thumb|Results by county: {{legend|#002255|Schneider—100%}} {{legend|#003380|Schneider—>90%}} ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Mac Schneider | party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | votes = 33545 | percentage = 99.78 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Write-Ins | party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | votes = 74 | percentage = 0.22 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 33619 | percentage = 100.00 }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== === Predictions === {| class="wikitable" |+ !Source !Ranking !As of |- |[[The Cook Political Report]]{{Cite news|url=https://cookpolitical.com/house-maps-0|title=House Maps|work=The Cook Political Report|access-date=2018-06-07|language=en}} | style="background:#f66" |{{sort|096|Solid R}} |June 1, 2018 |- |[[The Rothenberg Political Report]]{{Cite web|url=https://insideelections.com/state/south-dakota|title=South Dakota {{!}} Inside Elections|website=insideelections.com|language=en|access-date=2018-06-07}} | style="background:#f66" |{{sort|096|Solid R}} |June 1, 2018 |- |[[Sabato's Crystal Ball]]{{Cite web|url=http://www.centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/2018-house/|title=Larry J.
